blocking.section: Bootstrap and enrollment (Control-mode bootstrap steps 2-3, Figure 7)
blocking.issue: An operator cannot run the Control-mode bootstrap as written. Step 3 and Figure 7 end the second replica at `ruralz control join`. The CLI reference says join only obtains the peer certificate and runs BEFORE `ruralz control serve`, and it needs `--peer` and `--advertise`. So the replica is never started. Step 3 also needs an `admin` session in Ruralz Console, but step 2 creates no user and no source document defines how the first `admin` identity exists. Step 5 then needs `security-admin` (Ruralz Console Nodes row) for `ruralz node token`. The sequence stalls at step 3 for T3, T5 and T10, and T4 has the same gap (see also L1-1).
blocking.evidence: Doc line 405: "3. **More replicas.** An `admin` creates a one-time join token in Ruralz Console Settings; `ruralz control join` redeems it over 8092 and the leader adds a voter." Figure 7: "Op->>R2: ruralz control join with the token" with no serve step. CLI and API surface line 211: "`ruralz control join` runs on the new replica's host before `ruralz control serve`... redeems the one-time `admin` token from `--join-token-file`, issued by `/api/v1/replicas`"; line 137: "`--advertise HOST:8092` (required)". A grep of docs/architecture and docs/reference for a first-admin or bootstrap-admin mechanism finds none.
blocking.fix: Rewrite step 3 as follows: an `admin` obtains a join token from Ruralz Console Settings or `POST /api/v1/replicas`; on the new host, `ruralz control join --peer <leader>:8092 --advertise <self>:8092 --join-token-file <f>` stores the peer certificate; then `ruralz control serve` starts the replica, which the leader adds as a voter. Add the serve message to Figure 7. Add a step 2a naming how the first `admin` (and `security-admin`) principal is created, and add an Open question for it, e.g. OQ-deployment-topologies-11 (a) a one-time bootstrap credential printed or written by the first `ruralz control serve` (proposed), (b) an initial admin from process configuration, owner security-and-identity, Blocking: Yes, for Planned (M2).

blocking.section: Topology catalog (T10 bullets and Figure 6 caption) and Network and ports (flow table)
blocking.issue: The hybrid boundary is described as narrower than its dependencies make it. An operator using this section for T10 firewall rules and credentials would misconfigure it. Besides the Control Stream and Git reads, Control plane and GitOps has the customer's forge dial the managed side's 8090 with HMAC webhooks. Ruralz Console write-back pushes branches into the customer's Git, so the managed side holds Git write credentials. The builder's online Plugin check dials the customer's allowlisted OCI registry (L1-8 covers only this last part). The flow table also says Ruralz Control only reads Git.
blocking.evidence: Doc: "*Figure 6: hybrid topology; only the Control Stream and Git reads cross the boundary.*" and the flow row "Git object reads | Ruralz Control leader, CI | Git forge". Control plane and GitOps Figure 1: `gw -.->|"Git objects, push"| git`, `bld -.->|"online Plugin check"| oci`; "Forge webhooks at `/api/v1/hooks/git` need a per-source HMAC"; write-back: "submit commits an audited branch (author: the user)". Doc Network table 8090 row itself lists "forge webhooks".
blocking.fix: Change the Figure 6 caption to name every crossing: the Control Stream (Node to managed 8091), Git reads and write-back pushes (managed to customer forge), forge webhooks (customer forge to managed 8090) and the online Plugin check (managed to customer registry). Add those edges to Figure 6. Change the flow row to 'Git object reads and write-back pushes'. Add a T10 bullet saying the managed side holds Git read credentials, plus write credentials only if write-back is enabled. Widen OQ-deployment-topologies-10 to cover write-back credentials and private registries, or add a new OQ.

blocking.section: Topology catalog (T4, decision on OQ-system-overview-8) and Configuration delivery per topology (T4 row)
blocking.issue: The decision to make 'one bound namespace' an Environment's primary source leaves out three rules of Control plane and GitOps that a T4 operator will hit. First, a CRD source records a digest in place of a commit and shows as Drift. Second, it is refused for an Environment with `requireApproval` unless process configuration overrides it. Third, promotion moves a commit, never a digest, so it is undefined how a namespace-sourced `staging` promotes to `prod`. The doc owns OQ-system-overview-8, but it neither adopts nor amends these rules. As written, an operator binding a `prod` namespace with `requireApproval` (the RA-2 pattern) gets every change refused and cannot tell why.
blocking.evidence: Doc line 197: "Each Environment takes one primary source, a Git path or one bound namespace... `ruralz bundle push` stays the audited exception shown as Drift". Control plane and GitOps: "Two sources record a digest in place of a commit, pass `promotion.from` and `requireApproval` exactly like one and show as Drift" and "Both are refused for an Environment with `requireApproval` unless process configuration overrides it, which is audited." Pack 8.1: "Promotion | Moves a source commit, not a digest".
blocking.fix: Extend the OQ-system-overview-8 decision to say: (1) whether a namespace-primary Environment reports Drift, and if not, record it as a Control plane and GitOps amendment through an Open question; (2) that `requireApproval` refuses CRD changes unless process configuration overrides it, which is audited; (3) how `promotion.from` works when either Environment is namespace-sourced (for example, not allowed, with a new OQ for object-set promotion). Mirror (2) and (3) in the T4 row of Configuration delivery per topology.

blocking.section: Topology catalog (T4 chart object table, Node StatefulSet row)
blocking.issue: The row lets file-mode Nodes use an ephemeral `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}`. Scalability and distributed state makes persistent storage a MUST for any Node that may be rescheduled, because an `emptyDir` pod loses Last-Known-Good. For an OCI-pulling file-mode pod, 'if its registry is reachable at boot' cannot be guaranteed at deploy time. A pod rescheduled during a registry outage boots nothing and stays not ready, which defeats P9. The row contradicts a depends_on document.
blocking.evidence: Doc: "Node StatefulSet | A persistent volume for `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}`, which rescheduled Control-mode pods MUST keep (OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-7); file mode MAY use an ephemeral volume if its registry is reachable at boot". Scalability: "Nodes that may be rescheduled MUST keep `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}` on persistent storage, since an `emptyDir` pod loses its identity and Last-Known-Good (OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-7)."
blocking.fix: Limit the exception to file-mode pods whose Bundle is a locally mounted rendered directory (a ConfigMap or volume), because their source is present at every boot. Require a persistent volume for OCI-pull pods. Alternatively, keep the MAY but record it as a proposed amendment to Scalability's MUST under OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-7, and state the consequence: a rescheduled pod stays not ready during a registry outage.

blocking.section: Topology catalog (T4 chart object table, Secrets row) and Network and ports (flow table)
blocking.issue: The chart's only RBAC statement covers Node Secret reads. The flow table says Nodes read the Kubernetes API for `kubernetes` discovery. Traffic management defines that discovery as an EndpointSlice watch for a `service` in a configurable `namespace`, which needs `list` and `watch` on EndpointSlices in each target namespace. An operator who installs the chart as specified gets discovery Upstreams without Endpoints. The Ruralz Control side (CRD watch in bound namespaces, cluster-scoped Environment and Cluster CRDs, CRD status) has no RBAC row either (see L1-3).
blocking.evidence: Doc: "Secrets | Mounted as files for `secretRef` `provider: file`; `provider: kubernetes` needs `get` and `watch` in the Node's namespace only" and flow row "Secret and discovery reads | Nodes | Kubernetes API or Vault | With `provider: kubernetes`, `provider: vault` or `kubernetes` discovery". Traffic management: "Kubernetes | `discovery.type: kubernetes`, `service`, `namespace`, `port` | EndpointSlice watch".
blocking.fix: Replace the Secrets row with an 'RBAC' row that lists each principal. The Node ServiceAccount gets `get` and `watch` on Secrets in its own namespace (only with `provider: kubernetes`), plus `list` and `watch` on `endpointslices.discovery.k8s.io` in each namespace that Upstreams name (a Role per namespace, set through chart values, OQ-deployment-topologies-1). The `ruralz-control` ServiceAccount gets `list` and `watch` on the `ruralz.io` CRDs in bound namespaces, read on the cluster-scoped Environment and Cluster CRDs, and CRD status updates. State that nothing needs cluster-wide Secret access.
